numbering: Standard 700-verse canon; Chapter 13 has 34 verses and excludes Arjuna's alternate opening question.
sourceChapterWithLineNumbers:
1:   Krishna.
2:   Learn now, dear Prince! how, if thy soul be set
3:   Ever on Me--still exercising Yog,
4:   Still making Me thy Refuge--thou shalt come
5:   Most surely unto perfect hold of Me.
6:   I will declare to thee that utmost lore,
7:   Whole and particular, which, when thou knowest,
8:   Leaveth no more to know here in this world.
9: 
10:   Of many thousand mortals, one, perchance,
11:   Striveth for Truth; and of those few that strive--
12:   Nay, and rise high--one only--here and there--
13:   Knoweth Me, as I am, the very Truth.
14: 
15:   Earth, water, flame, air, ether, life, and mind,
16:   And individuality--those eight
17:   Make up the showing of Me, Manifest.
18: 
19:   These be my lower Nature; learn the higher,
20:   Whereby, thou Valiant One! this Universe
21:   Is, by its principle of life, produced;
22:   Whereby the worlds of visible things are born
23:   As from a Yoni. Know! I am that womb:
24:   I make and I unmake this Universe:
25:   Than me there is no other Master, Prince!
26:   No other Maker! All these hang on me
27:   As hangs a row of pearls upon its string.
28:   I am the fresh taste of the water; I
29:   The silver of the moon, the gold o' the sun,
30:   The word of worship in the Veds, the thrill
31:   That passeth in the ether, and the strength
32:   Of man's shed seed. I am the good sweet smell
33:   Of the moistened earth, I am the fire's red light,
34:   The vital air moving in all which moves,
35:   The holiness of hallowed souls, the root
36:   Undying, whence hath sprung whatever is;
37:   The wisdom of the wise, the intellect
38:   Of the informed, the greatness of the great.
39:   The splendour of the splendid. Kunti's Son!
40:   These am I, free from passion and desire;
41:   Yet am I right desire in all who yearn,
42:   Chief of the Bharatas! for all those moods,
43:   Soothfast, or passionate, or ignorant,
44:   Which Nature frames, deduce from me; but all
45:   Are merged in me--not I in them! The world--
46:   Deceived by those three qualities of being--
47:   Wotteth not Me Who am outside them all,
48:   Above them all, Eternal! Hard it is
49:   To pierce that veil divine of various shows
50:   Which hideth Me; yet they who worship Me
51:   Pierce it and pass beyond.
52: 
53:   I am not known
54:   To evil-doers, nor to foolish ones,
55:   Nor to the base and churlish; nor to those
56:   Whose mind is cheated by the show of things,
57:   Nor those that take the way of Asuras.[FN#12]
58: 
59:   Four sorts of mortals know me: he who weeps,
60:   Arjuna! and the man who yearns to know;
61:   And he who toils to help; and he who sits
62:   Certain of me, enlightened.
63: 
64:   Of these four,
65:   O Prince of India! highest, nearest, best
66:   That last is, the devout soul, wise, intent
67:   Upon "The One." Dear, above all, am I
68:   To him; and he is dearest unto me!
69:   All four are good, and seek me; but mine own,
70:   The true of heart, the faithful--stayed on me,
71:   Taking me as their utmost blessedness,
72:   They are not "mine,"but I--even I myself!
73:   At end of many births to Me they come!
74:   Yet hard the wise Mahatma is to find,
75:   That man who sayeth, "All is Vasudev!"[FN#13]
76: 
77:   There be those, too, whose knowledge, turned aside
78:   By this desire or that, gives them to serve
79:   Some lower gods, with various rites, constrained
80:   By that which mouldeth them. Unto all such--
81:   Worship what shrine they will, what shapes, in faith--
82:   'Tis I who give them faith! I am content!
83:   The heart thus asking favour from its God,
84:   Darkened but ardent, hath the end it craves,
85:   The lesser blessing--but 'tis I who give!
86:   Yet soon is withered what small fruit they reap:
87:   Those men of little minds, who worship so,
88:   Go where they worship, passing with their gods.
89:   But Mine come unto me! Blind are the eyes
90:   Which deem th' Unmanifested manifest,
91:   Not comprehending Me in my true Self!
92:   Imperishable, viewless, undeclared,
93:   Hidden behind my magic veil of shows,
94:   I am not seen by all; I am not known--
95:   Unborn and changeless--to the idle world.
96:   But I, Arjuna! know all things which were,
97:   And all which are, and all which are to be,
98:   Albeit not one among them knoweth Me!
99: 
100:   By passion for the "pairs of opposites,"
101:   By those twain snares of Like and Dislike, Prince!
102:   All creatures live bewildered, save some few
103:   Who, quit of sins, holy in act, informed,
104:   Freed from the "opposites,"and fixed in faith,
105:   Cleave unto Me.
106: 
107:   Who cleave, who seek in Me
108:   Refuge from birth[FN#14] and death, those have the Truth!
109:   Those know Me BRAHMA; know Me Soul of Souls,
110:   The ADHYATMAN; know KARMA, my work;
111:   Know I am ADHIBHUTA, Lord of Life,
112:   And ADHIDAIVA, Lord of all the Gods,
113:   And ADHIYAJNA, Lord of Sacrifice;
114:   Worship Me well, with hearts of love and faith,
115:   And find and hold me in the hour of death.
116: 
117:   HERE ENDETH CHAPTER VII. OF THE BHAGAVAD-GITA,
118:   Entitled "Vijnanayog,"
119:   Or "The Book of Religion by Discernment."

arnold.content:
Krishna.
  Learn now, dear Prince! how, if thy soul be set
  Ever on Me--still exercising Yog,
  Still making Me thy Refuge--thou shalt come
  Most surely unto perfect hold of Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.1 The Blessed Lord said O Arjuna, hear how you shall without doubt know Me fully, with the mind intent on Me, practising Yoga and taking refuge in Me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.1 "Lord Shri Krishna said: Listen, O Arjuna! And I will tell thee how thou shalt know Me in my Full perfection, practising meditation with thy mind devoted to Me, and having Me for thy refuge.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.1 The Blessed Lord said O Partha, hear how you, having the mind fixed on Me, practising the Yoga of Meditation and taking refuge in Me, will know Me with certainly and in fulness.

records.sanskrit:

records.iast:

records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
I will declare to thee that utmost lore,
  Whole and particular, which, when thou knowest,
  Leaveth no more to know here in this world.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.2 I shall declare to thee in full this knowledge combined with realisation, after knowing which nothing more here remains to be known.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.2 I will reveal to this knowledge unto thee, and how it may be realised; which, once accomplished, there remains nothing else worth having in this life.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.2 I shall tell you in detail of this Knowledge which is combined with realization, [From the statement, 'jnasyasi, you will know', in the earlier verse, one may conclude that the Lord is speaking of indirect or theoretical knowledge. The word 'idam, this' rules out such a conclusion; and it has also been said that this Knowledge is 'savijnanam, combined with direct experienece, realization'; it is Consciousness.] after experience which there remains nothing else here to be known again.

arnold.content:
Of many thousand mortals, one, perchance,
  Striveth for Truth; and of those few that strive--
  Nay, and rise high--one only--here and there--
  Knoweth Me, as I am, the very Truth.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.3 Among thousands of men, one perchance strives for perfection; even among those successful strivers, only one perchance knows Me in essence.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.3 Among thousands of men scarcely one strives for perfection, and even amongst those who gain occult powers, perchance but one knows me in truth.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.3 Among thousands of men a rare one endeavours for perfection. Even of the perfected ones who are diligent, one perchance knows Me in truth.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.4 Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect and egoism thus is My Nature divided eightfold.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.4 Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect and personality; this is the eightfold division of My Manifested Nature.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.4 This Prakrti of Mine is divided eight-fold thus: earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and also egoism.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.5 This is the inferior Prakriti, O mighty-armed (Arjuna); know thou as different from it My higher Prakriti (Nature), the very life-element, by which this world is upheld.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.5 This is My inferior Nature; but distinct from this, O Valiant One, know thou that my Superior Nature is the very Life which sustains the universe.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.5 O mighty-armed one, this is the inferior (Prakrti). Know the other Prakrti of Mine which, however, is higher than this, which has taken the from of individual souls, and by which this world is uphelp.

arnold.content:

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.6 Know that these two (Natures) are the womb of all beings. So I am the source and dissolution of the whole universe.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.6 It is the womb of all being; for I am He by Whom the worlds were created and shall be dissolved.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.6 Understand thus that all things (sentient and insentient) have these as their source. I am the origin as also the end of the whole Universe.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.7 There is nothing whatsoever higher than Me, O Arjuna. All this is strung on Me, as clusters of gems on a string.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.7 O Arjuna! There is nothing higher than Me; all is strung upon Me as rows of pearls upon a thread.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.7 O Dhananjaya, there is nothing else whatsoever higher than Myself. All this is strung on Me like pearls on a string.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.8 I am the sapidity in water, O Arjuna; I am the light in the moon and the sun; I am the syllable Om in all the Vedas, sound in ether and virility in men.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.8 O Arjuna! I am the Fluidity in water, the Light in the sun and in the moon. I am the mystic syllable Om in the Vedic scriptures, the Sound in ether, the Virility in man.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.8 O son of Kunti, I am the taste of water, I am the effulgence of the moon and the sun; (the letter) Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space, and manhood in men.

arnold.content:
The world--
  Deceived by those three qualities of being--
  Wotteth not Me Who am outside them all,
  Above them all, Eternal!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.13 Deluded by these Natures (states or things) composed of the three alities of Nature all this world does not know Me as distinct from them and immutable.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.13 The inhabitants of the world, misled by those natures which the Qualities have engendered, know not that I am higher than them all, and that I do not change.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.13 All this world, deluded as it is by these three things made of the gunas (alities), does not know Me who am transcendental to these and undecaying.

arnold.content:
Hard it is
  To pierce that veil divine of various shows
  Which hideth Me; yet they who worship Me
  Pierce it and pass beyond.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.14 Verily, this divine illusion of Mine, made up of the (three) alities (of Nature) is difficult to cross over; those who take refuge in Me alone, cross over this illusion.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.14 Verily, this Divine Illusion of Phenomenon manifesting itself in the Qualities is difficult to surmount. Only they who devote themselves to Me and to Me alone can accomplish it.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.14 Since this divine Maya of Mine which is constituted by the gunas is difficult to cross over, (therefore) those who take refuge in Me alone cross over this Maya.

records.sanskrit:
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः।
माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः ॥
records.iast:
na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ
māyayāpahṛtajñānā āsuraṃ bhāvamāśritāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
I am not known
  To evil-doers, nor to foolish ones,
  Nor to the base and churlish; nor to those
  Whose mind is cheated by the show of things,
  Nor those that take the way of Asuras.[FN#12]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.15 The evil-doers and the deluded who are the lowest of men do not seek Me; they whose knowledge is destroyed by illusion follow the ways of demons.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.15 The sinner, the ignorant, the vile, deprived of spiritual perception by the glamour of Illusion, and he who pursues a godless life - none of them shall find Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.15 The foolish evildoers, who are the most depraved among men, who are deprived of (their) wisdom by Maya, and who resort to demoniacal ways, do not take refuge in Me.

records.sanskrit:
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन।
आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ ॥
records.iast:
caturvidhā bhajante māṃ janāḥ sukṛtino.arjuna
ārto jijñāsurarthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Four sorts of mortals know me: he who weeps,
  Arjuna! and the man who yearns to know;
  And he who toils to help; and he who sits
  Certain of me, enlightened.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.16 Four kinds of virtuous men worship Me, O Arjuna, and they are the distressed, the seekr of knowledge, the seekr of wealth and the wise, O lord of the Bharatas.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.16 O Arjuna! The righteous who worship Me are grouped by stages: first, they who suffer, next they who desire knowledge, then they who thirst after truth, and lastly they who attain wisdom.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.16 O Arjuna, foremost of the Bharata dynasty, four classes of people of virtuous deeds adore Me: the afflicted, the seeker of Knowledge, the seeker of wealth and the man of Knowledge.

records.sanskrit:
तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते।
प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥
records.iast:
teṣāṃ jñānī nityayukta ekabhaktirviśiṣyate
priyo hi jñānino.atyarthamahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Of these four,
  O Prince of India! highest, nearest, best
  That last is, the devout soul, wise, intent
  Upon "The One." Dear, above all, am I
  To him; and he is dearest unto me!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.17 Of them the wise, ever steadfast and devoted to the One, excels (is the best); for I am exceedingly dear to the wise and he is dear to Me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.17 Of all of these, he who has gained wisdom, who meditates on Me without ceasing, devoting himself only to Me, he is the best; for by the wise man I am exceedingly beloved and the wise man, too, is beloved by Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.17 Of them, the man of Knowledge, endowed with constant steadfastness and one-pointed devotion, excels. For I am very much dear to the man of Knowledge, and he too is dear to Me.

records.sanskrit:
उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम्।
आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् ॥
records.iast:
udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tvātmaiva me matam
āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā māmevānuttamāṃ gatim
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
All four are good, and seek me; but mine own,
  The true of heart, the faithful--stayed on me,
  Taking me as their utmost blessedness,
  They are not "mine,"but I--even I myself!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.18 Noble indeed are all these; but I deem the wise man as My very Self; for, steadfast in mind he is established in Me alone as the supreme goal.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.18 Noble-minded are they all, but the wise man I hold as my own Self; for he, remaining always at peace with Me, makes me his final goal.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.18 All of these, indeed, are noble, but the man of Knowledge is the very Self. (This is) My opinion. For, with a steadfast mind, he is set on the path leading to Me alone who am the super-excellent Goal.

records.sanskrit:
बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते।
वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः ॥
records.iast:
bahūnāṃ janmanāmante jñānavānmāṃ prapadyate
vāsudevaḥ sarvamiti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
At end of many births to Me they come!
  Yet hard the wise Mahatma is to find,
  That man who sayeth, "All is Vasudev!"[FN#13]

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.19 At the end of many births the wise man comes to Me, realising that all this is Vaasudeva (the innermost Self); such a great soul (Mahatma) is very hard to find.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.19 After many lives, at last the wise man realises Me as I am. A man so enlightened that he sees God everywhere is very difficult to find.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.19 At the end of many births the man of Knowledge attains Me, (realizing) that Vasudeva is all. Such a high-souled one is very rare.

records.sanskrit:
कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः।
तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया ॥
records.iast:
kāmaistaistairhṛtajñānāḥ prapadyante.anyadevatāḥ
taṃ taṃ niyamamāsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
There be those, too, whose knowledge, turned aside
  By this desire or that, gives them to serve
  Some lower gods, with various rites, constrained
  By that which mouldeth them.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.20 Those whose wisdom has been rent away by this or that desire, go to other gods, following this or that rite, led by their own nature.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.20 They in whom wisdom is obscured by one desire or the other, worship the lesser Powers, practising many rites which vary according to their temperaments.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.20 People, deprived of their wisdom by desires for various objects and guided by their own nature, resort to other deities following the relevant methods.

records.sanskrit:
यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति।
तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् ॥
records.iast:
yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitumicchati
tasya tasyācalāṃ śraddhāṃ tāmeva vidadhāmyaham
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Unto all such--
  Worship what shrine they will, what shapes, in faith--
  'Tis I who give them faith! I am content!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.21 Whatsoever form any devotee desires to worship with faith that (same) faith of his I make firm and unflinching.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.21 But whatever the form of worship, if the devotee have faith, then upon his faith in that worship do I set My own seal.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.21 Whichever form (of a deity) any devotee wants to worship with faith, that very firm faith of his I strengthen.

records.sanskrit:
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते।
लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान्हि तान् ॥
records.iast:
sa tayā śraddhayā yuktastasyārādhanamīhate
labhate ca tataḥ kāmānmayaivavihitānhi tān
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
The heart thus asking favour from its God,
  Darkened but ardent, hath the end it craves,
  The lesser blessing--but 'tis I who give!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.22 Endowed with that faith, he engages in the worship of that (form) and from it he obtains his desire, these being verily ordained by Me (alone).

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.22 If he worships one form alone with real faith, then shall his desires be fulfilled through that only; for thus have I ordained.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.22 Being imbued with that faith, that person engages in worshipping that form, and he gets those very desired results therefrom as they are dispensed by Me alone.

records.sanskrit:
अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम्।
देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि ॥
records.iast:
antavattu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tadbhavatyalpamedhasām
devāndevayajo yānti madbhaktā yānti māmapi
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Yet soon is withered what small fruit they reap:
  Those men of little minds, who worship so,
  Go where they worship, passing with their gods.
  But Mine come unto me!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.23 Verily the reward (fruit) that accrues to those men of small intelligence is finite. The worshippers of the gods go to them, but My devotees come to Me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.23 The fruit that comes to men of limited insight is, after all, finite. They who worship the Lower Powers attain them; but those who worship Me come unto Me alone.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.23 That result of theirs who are of poor intellect is indeed limited. The worshippers of gods go to the gods. My devotees go to Me alone.

records.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः।
परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् ॥
records.iast:
avyaktaṃ vyaktimāpannaṃ manyante māmabuddhayaḥ
paraṃ bhāvamajānanto mamāvyayamanuttamam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Blind are the eyes
  Which deem th' Unmanifested manifest,
  Not comprehending Me in my true Self!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.24 The foolish think of Me, the Unmanifest, as having manifestation, knowing not My higher, immutable and most excellent nature.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.24 The ignorant think of Me, who am the Unmanifested Spirit, as if I were really in human form. They do not understand that My Superior Nature is changeless and most excellent.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.24 The unintelligent, unaware of My supreme state which is immutable and unsurpassable, think of Me as the unmanifest that has become manifest.

records.sanskrit:
नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः।
मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् ॥
records.iast:
nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ
mūḍho.ayaṃ nābhijānāti loko māmajamavyayam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Imperishable, viewless, undeclared,
  Hidden behind my magic veil of shows,
  I am not seen by all; I am not known--
  Unborn and changeless--to the idle world.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.25 I am not manifest to all (as I am) veiled by the Yoga-Maya. This deluded world does not know Me, the unborn and imperishable.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.25 I am not visible to all, for I am enveloped by the illusion of Phenomenon. This deluded world does not know Me as the Unborn and the Imperishable.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.25 Being enveloped by yoga-maya, I do not become manifest to all. This deluded world does not know Me who am birthless and undecaying.

records.sanskrit:
वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन।
भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन ॥
records.iast:
vedāhaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna
bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
But I, Arjuna! know all things which were,
  And all which are, and all which are to be,
  Albeit not one among them knoweth Me!

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.26 I know, O Arjuna, the beings of the past, the present and the future, but no one knows Me.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.26 I know, O Arjuna, all beings in the past, the present and the future; but they do not know Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.26 O Arjuna, I know the past and the present as also the future beings; but no one knows Me!

records.sanskrit:
इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत।
सर्वभूतानि सम्मोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥
records.iast:
icchādveṣasamutthena dvandvamohena bhārata
sarvabhūtāni sammohaṃ sarge yānti parantapa
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
By passion for the "pairs of opposites,"
  By those twain snares of Like and Dislike, Prince!
  All creatures live bewildered,

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.27 By the delusion of the pairs of opposites arising from desire and aversion, O Bharata, all beings are subject to delusion at birth, O Parantapa.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.27 O brave Arjuna! Man lives in a fairy world, deceived by the glamour of opposite sensations, infatuated by desire and aversion.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.27 O scion of the Bharata dynasty, O destroyer of foes, due to the delusion of duality arising from likes and dislikes, all creatures become bewildered at the time of their birth.

records.sanskrit:
येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम्।
ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः ॥
records.iast:
yeṣāṃ tvantagataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām
te dvandvamohanirmuktā bhajante māṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
save some few
  Who, quit of sins, holy in act, informed,
  Freed from the "opposites,"and fixed in faith,
  Cleave unto Me.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.28 But those men of virtuous deeds whose sins have come to an end, and who are freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites, worship Me, steadfast in their vows.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.28 But those who act righteously, in whom sin has been destroyed, who are free from the infatuation of the conflicting emotions, they worship Me with firm resolution.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.28 On the other hand, those persons who are of virtuous deeds, whose sin has come to an end, they, being free from the delusion of dulaity and firm in their convictions, adore Me.

records.sanskrit:
जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये।
ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् ॥
records.iast:
jarāmaraṇamokṣāya māmāśritya yatanti ye
te brahma tadviduḥ kṛtsnamadhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Who cleave, who seek in Me
  Refuge from birth[FN#14] and death, those have the Truth!
  Those know Me BRAHMA; know Me Soul of Souls,
  The ADHYATMAN; know KARMA, my work;

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.29 Those who strive for liberation from old age and death, taking refuge in Me, realise in full ï1thatï1 Brahman, the whole knowledge of the Self and all action.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.29 Those who make Me their refuge, who strive for liberation from decay and Death, they realise the Supreme Spirit, which is their own real Self, and in which all action finds its consummation.

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.29 Those who strive by resorting to Me for becoming free from old age and death, they know that Brahman, everything about the individual Self, and all about actions. [They know Brahman as being all the individual entities and all actions. This verse prescribes meditation on the alified Brahman for aspirants of the middle class. Verses beginning with the 14the speak about the reaization of the unalified Brahman by aspirants of the highest class.]

records.sanskrit:
साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः।
प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः ॥
records.iast:
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ
prayāṇakāle.api ca māṃ te viduryuktacetasaḥ
records.speaker: Krishna

arnold.content:
Know I am ADHIBHUTA, Lord of Life,
  And ADHIDAIVA, Lord of all the Gods,
  And ADHIYAJNA, Lord of Sacrifice;
  Worship Me well, with hearts of love and faith,
  And find and hold me in the hour of death.

witnesses.author: Swami Sivananda
witnesses.text: 7.30 Those who know Me with the Adhibhuta (pertaining to the elements), Adhidaiva (pertaining to the gods) and the Adhiyajna (pertaining to the sacrifice) know Me even at the time of death, steadfast in mind.

witnesses.author: Shri Purohit Swami
witnesses.text: 7.30 Those who see Me in the life of the world, in the universal sacrifice, and as pure Divinity, keeping their minds steady, they live in Me, even in the crucial hour of death."

witnesses.author: Swami Gambirananda
witnesses.text: 7.30 Those who know me as existing in the physical and the divine planes, and also in the context of the sacrifice, they of concentrated minds know Me even at the time of death.
